summary: node1 now serves CA-verified HTTPS at https://10.100.47.10:8443/. Certificates are checked daily and shortly after boot, renewed seven days before expiry, atomically installed, and picked up through a graceful nginx reload. The public trust anchor is /etc/pki/https-rotation/ca.crt; private keys remain root-only. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 were preserved.
actions_performed: Installed exact signed RHEL 10.0-compatible nginx 1.26.3 and OpenSSL 3.2.2 packages without upgrading the OS or kernel.
Created a local CA, restricted certificate storage, and a renewal script with locking, validation, atomic replacement, rollback, and graceful reload.
Configured nginx exclusively for the requested new listener on TCP 8443 and added a persistent firewalld rule while retaining enforcing SELinux.
Enabled a persistent systemd timer with daily checks and a post-boot check. Certificates use a 30-day lifetime and a seven-day renewal threshold.

Observed an automatic certificate rotation while 849 consecutive verified HTTPS requests completed with zero failures. The served certificate changed to the new on-disk certificate without replacing the nginx master process.
Restarted node1, proved its boot identity changed, and verified HTTPS, certificate data, firewall state, timer execution, and administrative services recovered.
Removed temporary test artifacts and confirmed no failed systemd units. The sole error-priority boot message is a kernel maintenance warning for ip_set.

evidence.summary: nginx listens on 8443, the managed-IP request returns HTTP 200 with the expected body, and TLS verification succeeds against the local CA.

evidence.requirement: Renew the certificate automatically before expiration
evidence.summary: The initial certificate was inside the seven-day renewal window; the enabled timer triggered automatically and replaced it with a new 30-day certificate.

evidence.requirement: Pick up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests
evidence.summary: The renewal validated and gracefully reloaded nginx. All 849 continuity requests succeeded, and the certificate served afterward exactly matched the new installed serial and fingerprint.
The validated timer is enabled for daily and post-boot checks; after reboot it ran successfully and confirmed the certificate remained beyond the renewal window.

Before/after evidence shows the same RHEL release and kernel. DNF only installed the required exact-version packages, CA/server keys are root-only, the nginx worker cannot read the CA key, and untrusted TLS/plain HTTP are rejected.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID 19062a82-6390-435d-a09f-4dba1593d529, received native reboot acknowledgement, observed temporary unavailability, then proved recovery under boot ID beb30d65-d816-43a4-985d-c4f378c20c2b with nginx, HTTPS data, certificate identity, firewall, timer, SSH, and security controls healthy.
Temporary probes were removed, no renewal temp directories or failed units remain, final HTTPS verification succeeds, and service journals show clean startup and renewal checks.
